The raw materials are put into the dried BN crucible and melted through a vacuum medium frequency induction melting furnace. Before melting, the furnace chamber is evacuated to 6 × 10−2 Pa and then fill it with pure argon gas to 6 × 104 Pa. The melted eutectic alloy is then superheated and poured into MgO crucible. The melting temperature is about 1823 K.

Another approximately 100 g ingot with a nominal composition of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is also prepared by a vacuum arc-melting furnace. A Ti-getter is used to assimilate the residual oxygen in the chamber. High purity elements (≥99.9%) are arc melted under argon atmosphere for at least five times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
Finally, the ~100 g ingot is re-arc melt and cast into a 15 mm × 15 mm × 60 mm copper mold.
